answer: Time-jitter clustering: every agent answers a coordinator pulse probe with its genuine latency signature. Identities whose pulse jitter matches too closely are judged to share one machine, so the ledger casts them into a single crystal cell and splits one emission across the whole cluster. Like marble, a forged fleet shows the same veining once pressure is applied: its pooled stake pays out once, making bulk sybil farming unprofitable while distinct hardware keeps full weight.
